title: GNSS Timing: North Shore Relocked, Iron Range and Cloquet Still Acquiring

fields.organization: Northern Lakes Transmission Operations, Fiber and Telecommunications Timing Team (Duluth control center)
fields.summary: NORTH_SHORE GPS clock has been LOCKED since 22:41:15 CDT. IRON_RANGE and CLOQUET are still timed from the backup network time server (Duluth, fiber ring), and their GPS receivers are still ACQUIRING: Iron Range has tracked 9 satellites at nominal C/N0 with no stable lock for 7 h 24 min.

fields.footer: 23:38:02 CDT MONITOR SUMMARY: 13 of 14 clocks on GPS or network time; 1 site pending return to GPS. *** EXERCISE *** Simulated values for exercise use only. They do not predict receiver performance.

instructorNote: Hand this page over together with the two transport items, read aloud or handed over at 23:40. First, the Northstar Heavy Haul dispatcher's email says the state oversize/overweight permit for the spare takes three business days (Mon 22 Mar), spring road restrictions start Friday so the route survey must be redone, and the spare cannot move before Tue 23 Mar. Second, the crane contractor's text says the 120-ton crane was released at 20:00, when the AT-1 crew went home, and its next slot is Wed 24 Mar, with a 2-day minimum and standby billed. Watch for: the TOM and RE book the permit and survey, decide on the crane slot, and log the spare as unavailable for at least a week in the T2 risk; TIME notices the '13 of 14 / 1 pending' summary does not match two sites still on network time, keeps Iron Range and Cloquet on the network source until GPS lock is stable, and plans the switch back one site at a time with the CRSS's agreement, never during switching or the Hartley relay review.
